Hi Alyssa — thanks for the detail and the grid. Looping in Karthik (solutions engineering) and Marissa (SE lead) so we can propose an operational cadence.

Quick notes from Redwood side and a proposed pattern:
- Target: 60-minute technical deep dive (45m demo + 15m Q&A). We can expand to 90m for hands-on labs but prefer to minimize heavy lab work during the session — we can follow up with a sandbox environment.
- SE coverage: Karthik can lead the demo; Marissa can run the architecture Q&A. For hands-on, we’ll provide a pre-seeded container so only a short setup is needed.
- Constraint: our primary GPU maintenance window is Tue 02:00–06:00 UTC (weekly patch), so avoid scheduling any critical hands-on when maintenance is likely.

Proposed rotating cadence (keeps the slot anchored to UTC but rotates local timing):
Option A (UTC anchor, rotates weekly):
  Week 1: 16:00 UTC — local times: 08:00 PST / 17:00 CET / 00:00 SGT (+1 day)
  Week 2: 00:00 UTC — local times: 16:00 PST (-1 day) / 01:00 CET / 08:00 SGT
  Week 3: 08:00 UTC — local times: 00:00 PST / 09:00 CET / 16:00 SGT
This pattern moves the comfortable time to each region every third week; sessions stay within the same weekday where possible.

Option B (split-series anchor — two short demos per week, regional-friendly):
  - Short session A: 15:00 UTC (late morning US / afternoon EU) — 45 mins (tech + Q&A)
  - Short session B: 23:30 UTC (evening EU / morning APAC) — 45 mins
Rotate which session is the primary hands-on each fortnight. This reduces very late/very early stretches for any single engineer.

I attached a small timezone matrix (timezone_matrix.csv) showing offsets and the rotated local times.

Can you confirm which option you prefer (A = full rotating single slot, B = two short regional-friendly slots)? If neither, tell us the top 3 weekdays/times that work for your architects and we’ll lock a recurring invite.

Thanks — I’ll hold off sending invites until we align.

—Vanessa

Thanks for looping me in. A few practical constraints and suggestions from the SE side:
- Preferred session length: 60 minutes for a focused deep dive. If NovaProspects wants a hands-on sandbox, we should schedule a separate 90-minute lab where we can provision a pre-warmed instance.
- Resource note: avoid scheduling the heavy demo (model inference benchmarks / live load test) during our Tue 02:00–06:00 UTC maintenance. If Option A lands on 00:00 UTC in any week, that conflicts with our weekly patch — so we should either shift the anchor by +2 hours or pick Option B.
- Roster: I can cover the demo for Week 1/3 slots; Marissa can cover Week 2 (rotating). For APAC-favored sessions, we should have a backup SE on call (Marissa).
- Recording & artifacts: we will record, share the slide deck, and a short runbook for follow-ups.

My vote: Option B — two short sessions reduces the maintenance collision risk and makes it easier to bring in different regional SEs without long nights.

Karthik
